priorities.title: Keep account actions from resizing the directory
priorities.finding: Desktop Manage expands a roughly 62px row to 461px, re-centers identity values and changes column widths; phone expansion confines actions to a narrow right column. This disrupts an existing account-management workflow. It is substantial layout friction, not proven task failure or an authorization defect.
priorities.fix: Keep the existing permitted action list and triggers, but put desktop disclosure outside table sizing (a compact anchored overlay with existing accessible/native handling) and give phone actions the available block width. Preserve operation-bound step-up, delegation filtering, destructive separation and focus handling. No new actions or backend work.
priorities.scope: Primary meaningful visual correction; independent dissatisfaction is rooted here, not in a tiny cohort shortfall.

priorities.title: Make the existing security setup page easier to scan
priorities.finding: Five coequal enclosing cards and large empty-status bands make this unconfigured setup screen heavier than Recovery task views; Allow this phone appears checked above an empty phone list without clear future-pairing context.
priorities.fix: Use flatter titled sections and compact empty states for the same controls; visually associate the existing sign-on checkbox with the phone-pairing action and clarify its scope with existing factual behavior. Keep all factor choices, authorization and enrollment behavior.
priorities.scope: Presentation of current setup only; do not select a new authentication policy or change the checkbox default.

priorities.title: Clarify existing directory/connection empty workflows on phones
priorities.finding: App connections clips its header and names three setup routes beside only Manage launcher cards; Groups puts dense policy text before Create group; Users repeats six label/value lines per account.
priorities.fix: Adapt the current app-connections table to readable phone blocks or visibly signposted horizontal scrolling; make the existing setup route discoverable from its empty state, keep exact policy consequences available near the relevant group action, and tighten repeated account metadata without hiding fields or permissions.
priorities.scope: Reuse existing routes/controls and preserve factual/security copy. No new provisioning features, bulk actions or backend redesign.
